references.text: Earlier in the chapter, the prohibition against Ammonites and Moabites entering the assembly of the Lord is mentioned, providing context for the rule concerning the third generation.
The preceding verse mentions Edomites and Egyptians, and verse 9 (verse 8 in some translations) states that their children in the third generation may enter the assembly of the Lord.
Refers to God's punishment extending to the third and fourth generations for those who hate Him, a parallel to the generational principle.
Reiterates the principle that the Lord punishes the sins of the parents upon the children to the third and fourth generation.
Nehemiah reads the law stating that Ammonites and Moabites should not enter the assembly of God, which refers to this passage in Deuteronomy.
Ruth's genealogy shows how a Moabite woman was integrated into Israel through the generations, relevant to the rules concerning generations and belonging.
